---
title: "`ev_theme()` — locked palette & ggplot theme"
---

## Purpose

Return the package's locked colour palette and ggplot2 theme as one list, so
every volcano and ring shares identical colours and styling.

## How it works

Builds a named palette and a `theme_minimal()`-based theme. The palette hex codes
are **locked** in source so a ggplot2 update can never silently shift the
up/down/ns colours or the NES scale. The returned list has three elements:

- `base_size` — the numeric base font size
- `theme` — `theme_minimal(base_size)` with minor grid removed and the legend at
  the bottom
- `palette` — `up = #D6604D` (red), `down = #4393C3` (blue), `ns = grey70`, and
  `nes_scale = c("#08306B", "white", "#67000D")` (diverging blue → white → red
  for NES)

Only the `"default"` palette exists in v1; any other name aborts.

## When to use

You rarely call it directly — every plotting function takes `theme = ev_theme()`
as a default. Call it to inspect the locked hex codes or to pass a larger
`base_size` to all panels at once.

## Parameters & defaults

| Argument | Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `base_size` | `11` | readable default; raise for large figures |
| `palette` | `"default"` | the only locked palette in v1; unknown names abort |

## Literature

No method-specific citation; see [methods](../methods.qmd).

## Example

```r
th <- ev_theme(base_size = 13)
th$palette$up        # "#D6604D"
ev_volcano(dep, "CTLvMITO", theme = th)
```
